task: Read-only review of Jackin reduced-color/modal dialog patch. No source edits; no capture roots or shared test data touched.

findings.finding: The change adds 1,600+ lines of fixed Plate cell/text data for Info and Cancel dialogs, paints them through low-level coordinates/raw RGB, and selects a special path at exactly 120x40 for non-truecolor. It is a production replay/plate path and application-owned rendering, not component composition. It also hardcodes text/content, so changed data, labels, or adjacent size cannot flow through shared components. Do not accept or merge this patch as a reusable-component fix merely because the 120x40 frame matches.

recolor_pair always calls mark_area(area,None); CellRoles::patch(None) returns default roles. Thus an identity/no-op recolor erases semantic fg/bg role metadata across the clip. Later layer composition/backdrop decisions that depend on roles change even though visible cell colors did not. Keep roles for unchanged channels/cells; when intentionally translating colors, translate semantic roles explicitly or mark only changed channels as unowned. Add a visible behavior regression through a semantic-role cell -> recolor_pair(identity) -> dim/composite and compare against no recolor.

Reduced-color behavior infers semantic surfaces and controls by exact RGB values (`button_rgb`, `blank_black`, hard-coded RGB-to-index maps and text color comparisons). The color-level/NO_COLOR branches are capability handling, but choosing widget meaning from exact resolved ink is not. Alternate theme values or another widget using those colors are misclassified. Carry role/surface/state provenance through the cell/layer and resolve reduced color from semantic tokens; do not duplicate raw-RGB palette conversion in app rendering.

The implementation assigns DIM as the only modifier in reduced/NO_COLOR backdrop paths, which discards prior modifiers. However, the frozen baseline backdrop implementation (`src/ui/ctx.rs` 658–688 per independent parent inspection) intentionally replaces modifiers with the backdrop result; therefore the prior-modifier loss alone is not a proven parity violation. The adjacent code comment "NO_COLOR only sets dim" is ambiguous against this replacement contract. Do not treat as a required fix without a frame-level baseline mismatch; clarify the comment/contract if this branch remains.
